```{r}
#| label: setup
source(here::here("R", "functions.R"))
source(here::here("R", "plot_functions.R"))

db_dir     <- here::here("data", "processed")
stocks     <- readr::read_csv(file.path(db_dir, "stocks.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
timeseries <- readr::read_csv(file.path(db_dir, "timeseries.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
dd         <- readr::read_csv(file.path(db_dir, "data_dictionary.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Summary

This project combines two open sources into a small, documented database for ten British Columbia stocks. It applies simple written rules to describe each stock's status, its history, and the gaps in the evidence. It is a learning project by an epidemiologist who is new to fisheries science. It does not replicate DFO's methods or those of any seafood recommendation program, and it makes no recommendations.

## Data sources

| Source | What it provides | Version | Licence |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| DFO Sustainability Survey for Fisheries | Official status zone (Healthy, Cautious, Critical, Uncertain), reference point descriptions, management plans | 2024 results | Open Government Licence, Canada |
| RAM Legacy Stock Assessment Database | Assessment time series (biomass, catch, ratios to MSY) and reference points | v4.66, assessment-only | CC BY 4.0 |
| DFO Commercial Seafisheries Landings | Landings by species group, used only as background | 1990 to 2024 | Open Government Licence, Canada |

## Data tiers

Stocks differ in how much public evidence exists. Each stock is assigned a tier, and the tier decides which plots and caveats it gets.

| Tier | Meaning | Stocks |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A | Biomass and fishing pressure relative to MSY | Sablefish, Pacific halibut |
| B | Biomass relative to MSY only | Pacific cod (5ABCD) |
| C | Biomass and catch trends, no MSY ratios | Five Pacific herring areas |
| D | DFO status zone only, no assessment time series compiled | Spot prawn, Dungeness crab |

## A common indicator

Stocks use different reference points, so they cannot be compared directly. For every stock with a time series, this project divides biomass by that stock's **limit reference point (LRP)**, the level below which DFO considers serious harm to be occurring. A value below 1 means below the limit. The limits are taken or derived from RAM Legacy and are approximate.

```{r}
#| label: lrp-table
stocks |>
  filter(!is.na(lrp_basis)) |>
  transmute(
    Stock       = unname(stock_short[stock_id]),
    `Limit used` = lrp_basis,
    Value       = if_else(lrp_unit == "MT", paste(comma(round(lrp_value)), "t"),
                          paste0(lrp_value, " \u00d7 Bmsy"))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Cross-checks

**Herring limits, RAM versus DFO.** The LRP implied by RAM's 2018 values is compared with the value DFO reported in the 2024 survey, extracted automatically from the survey text.

```{r}
#| label: herring-check
stocks |>
  filter(species == "Pacific herring") |>
  mutate(dfo_txt = str_extract(lrp_description, "[0-9]{1,3}(,[0-9]{3})+(?= tonnes)"),
         dfo_num = parse_number(dfo_txt)) |>
  transmute(
    Stock                     = unname(stock_short[stock_id]),
    `RAM: 0.3 x SSB0 (t)`     = comma(round(lrp_value)),
    `DFO 2024 survey (t)`     = dfo_txt,
    Difference                = percent((lrp_value - dfo_num) / dfo_num, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

**Sablefish.** RAM's spawning biomass at MSY (22,820 t) is within 0.5% of the Bmsy reported in DFO's 2024 survey (22,720 t).

**Latest indicator versus DFO's 2024 zone.** A stock below its limit should be in the Critical zone; a stock above it should be Cautious or Healthy.

```{r}
#| label: agreement
timeseries |>
  filter(metric == "b_lrp") |>
  group_by(stock_id) |>
  slice_max(year, n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(select(stocks, stock_id, dfo_status_zone), by = "stock_id") |>
  transmute(
    Stock            = unname(stock_short[stock_id]),
    `Latest year`    = year,
    `Biomass / LRP`  = number(value, accuracy = 0.01),
    `DFO 2024 zone`  = coalesce(dfo_status_zone, "Not in survey"),
    Consistent       = case_when(
      is.na(dfo_status_zone) ~ "No zone to compare",
      (value < 1) == (dfo_status_zone == "Critical") ~ "Yes",
      TRUE ~ "No"
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Downloads

- [stocks.csv](data/processed/stocks.csv): one row per stock
- [timeseries.csv](data/processed/timeseries.csv): long-format time series, one row per stock, year, and metric
- [landings.csv](data/processed/landings.csv): BC commercial landings by species group
- [data_dictionary.csv](data/processed/data_dictionary.csv): every field in every table

## How it is built

All steps are R scripts in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/emmabranch/bc-fish-stock-status), run in order:

1. `01_download.R`: downloads the raw files.
2. `04_build_database.R`: builds the tidy tables and data dictionary.
3. `06_harmonise_lrp.R`: adds the biomass-to-limit indicator and runs the cross-checks.
4. `07_make_figures.R` and `08_map_cards.R`: figures, map, and cards.
5. `09_render_reports.R`: renders one parameterised 2-page PDF per stock.
6. `10_make_site_files.R`, then `quarto render`: builds this website.

## Limitations

- RAM Legacy copies published assessments, so the time series end between 2018 and 2021 and may not match DFO's latest advice.
- Limit reference points used for the common indicator are approximate, and some are derived rather than official.
- Point estimates only. Assessment uncertainty is not shown.
- Map pins mark general areas, not stock boundaries.
- National landings data group several BC species together, so they are not used for stock-level conclusions.
- Spot prawn and Dungeness crab have no compiled time series; their status here relies entirely on DFO's survey response.
